description: We are TriNova, a team of three enthusiastic students passionate about science, technology and space exploration. We are curious learners who enjoy sharing ideas, solving problems and exploring innovative solutions. We believe in teamwork, creativity and learning new things. Through NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to turn our ideas into meaningful solutions and gain valuable experience while exploring the wonders of space and science.
summary: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a web-based learning experience that lets kids aged 8-14 train like an astronaut. Players complete five missions: Launch, Orbit, Spacewalk, Mars Landing and Return. Each mission has a short briefing built from real NASA imagery, a timed decision-based simulation where choices change the outcome, and a debrief that awards badges. Players rise from Cadet to Commander, and a crew mode lets 2-4 players share roles such as Commander, Engineer, Medic and Navigator. The project addresses the challenge by turning space training into something students can practise, not just watch. It matters because few students can reach space camps or simulators, and our trainer is designed to be inclusive, with read-aloud support, colour-blind-safe design and low-bandwidth use.
details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a web-based trainer for kids aged 8-14. Players complete five missions: Launch, Orbit, Spacewalk, Mars Landing and Return. Each mission has three steps. Learn is a 60-second briefing built from real NASA imagery. Simulate is a timed decision scenario where the player's choices change the outcome. Debrief shows what worked, lets the player retry, and awards a mission badge. Badges raise the player's rank from Cadet to Pilot, Specialist and Commander.

Benefits and impact: Students practise the decisions astronauts make instead of only watching videos. Crew mode lets 2-4 players share roles (Commander, Engineer, Medic, Navigator) to build teamwork. It is designed to be inclusive, with read-aloud support, colour-blind-safe design and low-bandwidth use, so students without access to space camps or simulators can still take part.
